istqb.d: The International Software Testing Qualifications Board — the body behind the most widely recognized software-testing certification scheme.
istqb.w: An ISTQB cert is the credential recruiters filter on most often in QA/test automation postings — worth tracking news from the board directly.

mcdc.d: Modified Condition/Decision Coverage — a strict test-coverage criterion requiring every condition in a compound boolean to be shown, on its own, to change the outcome.
mcdc.w: ISO 26262 requires it at higher safety levels — a term worth recognizing instantly in automotive/embedded QA postings.

csms.d: Cyber Security Management System — the certified process UNECE R155 requires carmakers to run across a vehicle's whole life.
csms.w: Regulatory floor under automotive security testing — demand for these skills is written into law, not fashion.

lang_dieversicherung.w: Germany runs on mandatory insurance for almost everything — health, liability, often even contents insurance is expected.

lang_dieanmeldung.d: Residence registration — the mandatory first step after moving to a German address.
lang_dieanmeldung.w: Everything else (bank account, tax ID, health insurance) depends on this being done first.

lang_dergegenstand.w: “Ich schließe meine persönlichen Gegenstände im Schwimmbad lieber in ein Fach ein.”

lang_gegenüber.w: “Das Geschäft liegt direkt gegenüber der Post.”

lang_dasgeheimnis.w: “Das kann ich dir nicht sagen. Das ist ein Geheimnis.”

lang_geheim.w: “Das ist geheim. Du darfst es niemandem sagen.”

lang_gehen.w: “Ich gehe jeden Morgen zu Fuß zur Arbeit.”

lang_dergehsteigd.w: “Das Fahrradfahren auf dem Gehsteig ist nicht erlaubt.”

lang_diegeldbörse.w: “Ich habe nur Kleingeld in meiner Geldbörse.”

lang_diegelegenheit.w: “Das Fest ist eine gute Gelegenheit, unsere Freunde zu sehen.”

lang_gelingen.w: “Es ist mir gelungen, meinen Chef zu überzeugen.”

maitraka.d: The dynasty that ruled Saurashtra from Vallabhi, roughly 475-776 CE, beginning as Gupta generals and becoming independent kings as the Gupta empire fell apart.
maitraka.w: They funded Vallabhi into a university that rivalled Nalanda — the reason your wife's home region was, for three centuries, one of the intellectual capitals of Asia.

jyotirlinga.d: One of twelve shrines across India where Shiva is held to have manifested as a pillar of light; Somnath in Saurashtra is counted as the first.
jyotirlinga.w: Explains why Somnath's repeated destruction and rebuilding carried (and still carries) stakes far beyond one building.

kathiawar.d: The British-era name for the Saurashtra peninsula, administered as an Agency of over two hundred separate princely states before 1947.
kathiawar.w: The reason dialects, dress and cuisine vary so sharply over short distances across the region your wife's family is from.

bandhani.d: A tie-dye technique where cloth is tied into thousands of tiny points before dyeing, producing fine dotted patterns — a Saurashtra/Gujarat textile signature.
bandhani.w: One of the region's most recognizable cultural exports — worth being able to name when you see it.

baserate.d: How common something actually is in the whole population being tested — the figure that determines whether a positive test result is likely to be a true or false positive.
baserate.w: The single most-forgotten number in statistics; ignoring it is why a 99% accurate test for a rare condition is usually wrong when it says yes.

redsupergiant.d: A star near the end of its life that has swollen to enormous size — Betelgeuse is roughly a thousand times the Sun's width.
redsupergiant.w: Red supergiants end their lives as supernovae — Betelgeuse's, whenever it happens, will be visible in daylight from Earth.

lateralmovement.d: The quiet phase of a real intrusion where an attacker who has already gained access sits still, harvests credentials, and works sideways toward something valuable, often for weeks or months.
lateralmovement.w: The part of a cyberattack that actually does the damage — and the part the "someone types furiously" media picture leaves out entirely.

hypothermia.d: Dangerously low core body temperature, announcing itself in order — shivering, then clumsiness and slurred speech, then confusion.
hypothermia.w: Kills in temperatures well above freezing given wet clothes and wind — the real cold-weather risk in northern Germany, not snow and ice.

crypto.d: A thick-walled parasite cyst that survives normal chemical water disinfection (chlorine, iodine) far better than bacteria or viruses do.
crypto.w: The reason boiling and filtering are both still needed alongside chemical treatment — no single water-purification method covers everything.

wgb.d: Your landlord's signed confirmation of the date you moved in — mandatory since 2015 and required before any Anmeldung appointment can proceed.
wgb.w: Without this exact document the registration counter cannot help you, no matter what else you bring.

meldebescheinigung.d: The certificate of registration issued once your Anmeldung is complete — proof of your registered address for banks, employers and authorities.
meldebescheinigung.w: Ask for a couple of extra copies at the appointment; you will be asked for one again soon after.

swift.d: The messaging network banks use to instruct each other to debit and credit accounts they already hold — no money physically crosses a border, only messages do.
swift.w: Explains why a traditional international transfer takes days and passes through several institutions, each potentially taking a fee.

neft.d: National Electronic Funds Transfer — one of India's domestic payment rails, settling in batches through the day with no upper limit.
neft.w: One of three rails (with RTGS and IMPS) a transfer to India lands on — knowing which one explains how fast it actually arrives.

spread.d: The gap between the true mid-market exchange rate and the rate you're actually given on a transfer — usually the real cost, not the stated fee.
spread.w: Compare the rate you got against the mid-market rate that day; that gap plus the fee is what a transfer to India actually cost you.

transpiration.d: Evaporation of water from leaf pores (stomata), which puts the whole water column from root to leaf under tension and pulls water upward.
transpiration.w: The mechanism behind how a tree lifts water a hundred metres with no moving parts — suction alone could never do it.

endosymbiosis.d: The theory that mitochondria and chloroplasts began as free-living bacteria engulfed by another cell roughly two billion years ago, and kept rather than digested.
endosymbiosis.w: Explains why mitochondria have their own bacterial-type DNA and divide on their own schedule — direct evidence sits inside every one of your cells.

ketoazidose.d: Diabetic ketoacidosis — a dangerous build-up of blood acid produced when the body, lacking insulin, burns fat for fuel and generates ketones faster than it can clear them.
ketoazidose.w: The single most important pump-related risk to understand: it can begin within hours of a cannula failure, and can occur even with a near-normal glucose reading.

lang_gemeinsam.w: “Du musst die Wohnung renovieren? Ich helfe dir. Wir können das gemeinsam machen.”

lang_diegemeinschaft.w: “Rauchen ist in den Gemeinschafts-räumen nicht erlaubt.”

lang_dasgemüse.w: “Wir kaufen das Gemüse direkt beim Bauern.”

lang_genauso.w: “Katarina sieht genauso aus wie ihre Schwester.”

lang_genehmigen.w: “Mein Chef hat mir sechs Wochen Urlaub genehmigt.”

lang_diegeneration.w: “In diesem Haus wohnen drei Generationen zusammen.”
